rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a good-quality expanded blastocyst and compact ICM/cohesive TE, but it overstates image-derived certainty, introduces questionable details (e.g., nearing hatching/absence of zona, no collapse) and relies heavily on the provided 3AA grade.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, oocyte yield, BMI, semen parameters, prior IVF history, lifestyle, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality and prognosis.

Overall logic is structured, but there are internal inconsistencies: it calls the embryo 3AA yet also 'fully expanded/nearing hatching,' labels TE as 'good-to-fair' despite AA, and gives somewhat shifting probability/live birth estimates.

Generally aligned with IVF practice: appropriate emphasis on SET in a 25-year-old with a high-quality day-5 blastocyst, caution against unproven add-ons, and reasonable comments on PGT-A not being routine. Minor overemphasis on 14 mm endometrium as a concern without stronger indication.

Provides practical recommendations for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, avoiding unnecessary add-ons, and future uterine/endometrial review if failure occurs. Useful, though some suggestions remain somewhat generic.
